verses_en.wbw: svarūpera kare dhari — holding Svarupa's hand; bale kām̐di gaurahari — weeping, Gaurahari says; bihane — without; āmāra śyāma rāya — My Shyama; biphale bañcilum̐ niśi — I have spent the night in vain; astamita bhela śaśī — the moon has set; e parāṇa phāṭi majhu yāya — My heart is breaking

verses_en.text:
(Refrain) Where is My beloved Shyama?
The bed of flowers has wilted, the garland has withered —
I have not tasted the honey of Shyama's love.
verses_en.orig:
কোথায় আমার শ্যাম বঁধু ।
ফুল-শেজ বাসি ভেল ফুলহার শুখাওল
না মিলল শ্যাম-প্রেমমধু ॥ ধ্রু ॥
verses_en.translit:
kothāya āmāra śyāma bam̐dhu |
phula-śeja bāsi bhela phulahāra śukhāola
nā milala śyāma-premamadhu || dhru ||
verses_en.wbw: kothāya āmāra śyāma bām̐dhu — where is My beloved Shyama; phula-śeja bāsi bhela — the bed of flowers has gone stale; phulahāra śukhāola — the garland has withered; nā milala — was not found; śyāma-premamadhu — the honey of Shyama's love

verses_en.text:
Come, Svarupa, let us go to the waters of the Suradhuni —
let us set all this afloat.
Let honour and family be lost — I shall live no more:
I shall leap into the water and give up My life.*
verses_en.orig:
চল রে স্বরূপ চল যাই সুরধুনী-জল
এ সকল দেই ভাসাইয়া ।
গেল যাক কুলমান আর না রাখিব প্রাণ
তেজিব সলিলে ঝাঁপ দিয়া ॥
verses_en.translit:
cala re svarūpa cala yāi suradhunī-jala
e sakala dei bhāsāiyā |
gela yāka kulamāna āra nā rākhiba prāṇa
tejiba salile jhām̐pa diyā ||
verses_en.wbw: cala re svarūpa — come, Svarupa; cala yāi — let us go; suradhunī-jala — to the waters of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); e sakala dei bhāsāiyā — let us set all this afloat; gela yāka kulamāna — let family honour be gone; āra nā rākhiba prāṇa — I shall not keep My life; tejiba salile — I shall give it up in the water; jhām̐pa diyā — leaping in
notes: Radha's words in separation: "let honour and family be lost" is a sign of prema that gives up for Krishna everything the world

verses_en.text: That dark moon of Mine — in whose bower does He spend the night?
verses_en.orig:
আমার সে কালশশী কার কুঞ্জে বঞ্চে নিশি
কাঁহে মুঝে ভেলত বৈমুখ ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে এ দুখে পরাণ দহে
কাঁহা মিটায়ব হিয়া-দুখ ॥
verses_en.translit:
āmāra se kālaśaśī kāra kuñje bañce niśi
kām̐he mujhe bhelata baimukha |
bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe e dukhe parāṇa dahe
kām̐hā miṭāyaba hiyā-dukha ||
verses_en.wbw: āmāra se kālaśaśī — that dark moon of Mine; kāra kuñje bañce niśi — in whose bower does He spend the night; kām̐he mujhe — why from Me; bhelata baimukha — has He turned away; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; e dukhe parāṇa dahe — in this sorrow the heart burns; kām̐hā miṭāyaba hiyā-dukha — where shall I ease the pain of the heart

padas.ref: Нарахари (Саркар), ПК 1746 «আরে মোর গৌর কিশোর। নাহি জানে দিবানিশি»
padas.title: Смех без причины: Господь в разлуке ищет Владыку жизни
padas.summary: Не различая дня и ночи, Гаура смеётся без причины, громко поёт, спрашивая: «Где Мой Владыка жизни?», дрожит, прыгает, пляшет с воздетыми руками, бессвязно говорит, плачет с закрытыми глазами; поэт: таким Он стал из любви Радхи.

verses.text:
(Припев) Ах, мой юный Гаура!
Не различая дня и ночи, Он смеётся без причины —
Господь потерян в смятении сердца.
verses.orig:
আরে মোর গৌর কিশোর ।
নাহি জানে দিবানিশি কারণ বিহনে হাসি
মনের ভরমে পহুঁ ভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥
verses.translit:
āre mora gaura kiśora |
nāhi jāne dibāniśi kāraṇa bihane hāsi
manera bharame pahum̐ bhora || dhru ||
verses.wbw: аре мора гаура кишора — ах, мой юный Гаура; нахи джане дибаниши — не различает дня и ночи; карана бихане хаси — смеётся без причины; манера бхараме — в смятении сердца; паху бхора — Господь потерян

verses.text:
То Он громко поёт — у кого, о чём спрашивает Господь? —
«Где Мой Владыка жизни?»
То всё тело Его дрожит, как от холода, то Он прыгает:
«Где Мне найти Его? Куда идти? С кем?»*
verses.orig:
ক্ষেণে উচ্চ-স্বরে গায় কারে পহুঁ কি সুধায়
কোথায় আমার প্রাণনাথ ।
ক্ষেণে শীতে অঙ্গ কম্প ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে দেই লম্ফ
কাঁহা পাঙ যাঙ কার সাথ ॥
verses.translit:
kṣeṇe ucca-svare gāya kāre pahum̐ ki sudhāya
kothāya āmāra prāṇanātha |
kṣeṇe śīte aṅga kampa kṣeṇe kṣeṇe dei lampha
kām̐hā pāṅa yāṅa kāra sātha ||
verses.wbw: кшене учча-сваре гая — то громко поёт; каре паху ки судхая — у кого, о чём спрашивает Господь; котхая амара пранатха — где мой Владыка жизни; кшене шите анга кампа — то тело дрожит, как от холода; кшене кшене деи ламфа — то прыгает; канха пана — где найду; яна кара сатха — куда пойду, с кем
notes: Слова Радхи в разлуке: Она ищет Кришну и не знает, куда идти. Дрожь — саттвика-бхава; в ПК пада открывает раздел о

verses.text:
То, воздев руки, пляшет, кружась и кружась,
то вновь и вновь бессвязно говорит;
то закрывает глаза и плачет: «О Натха!»,
то вновь и вновь терзается.
verses.orig:
ক্ষেণে ঊর্দ্ধবাহু করি নাচি বুলে ফিরি ফিরি
ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে করয়ে প্রলাপ ।
ক্ষেণে আঁখিযুগ মুন্দে হা নাথ বলিয়া কান্দে
ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে করয়ে সন্তাপ ॥
verses.translit:
kṣeṇe ūrddhabāhu kari nāci bule phiri phiri
kṣeṇe kṣeṇe karaye pralāpa |
kṣeṇe ām̐khiyuga munde hā nātha baliyā kānde
kṣeṇe kṣeṇe karaye santāpa ||
verses.wbw: кшене урдхва-баху кари — то, воздев руки; начи буле пхири пхири — пляшет, кружась и кружась; кшене кшене карайе пралапа — то вновь и вновь бессвязно говорит; кшене анкхиюга мунде — то закрывает глаза; ха натха болия канде — плачет: «О Натха!»; кшене кшене карайе сантапа — то вновь и вновь терзается

verses.text: Говорит Нарахари Дас: ах, мой Гаурахари
verses.orig:
কহে দাস নরহরি আরে মোর গৌরহরি
রাধার পিরিতে হৈল হেন ।
ঐছন করিয়া চিতে কলিযুগ উদ্ধারিতে
বঞ্চিত হইলুঁ মুঞি কেন ॥
verses.translit:
kahe dāsa narahari āre mora gaurahari
rādhāra pirite haila hena |
aichana kariyā cite kaliyuga uddhārite
bañcita hailum̐ muñi kena ||
verses.wbw: кахе даса нарахари — говорит Нарахари Дас; аре мора гаурахари — ах, мой Гаурахари; радхара пирите хаила хена — стал таким из любви Радхи; аичхана кария чите — решив так в сердце; калиюга уддхарите — спасти век Кали; банчита хаилун мунни кена — почему я обделён

verses_en.text:
(Refrain) Ah, my youthful Gaura!
Not knowing day from night, He laughs without cause —
the Lord is lost in the bewilderment of His heart.
verses_en.orig:
আরে মোর গৌর কিশোর ।
নাহি জানে দিবানিশি কারণ বিহনে হাসি
মনের ভরমে পহুঁ ভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥
verses_en.translit:
āre mora gaura kiśora |
nāhi jāne dibāniśi kāraṇa bihane hāsi
manera bharame pahum̐ bhora || dhru ||
verses_en.wbw: are mora gaura kishora — ah, my youthful Gaura; nahi jane dibanishi — knows not day or night; karana bihane hasi — laughing without cause; manera bharame — in the bewilderment of the mind; pahun bhora — the Lord is lost

verses_en.text:
Now He sings aloud — of whom, of what does the Lord ask? —
"Where is the Lord of My life?"
Now His whole body trembles as with cold, now He leaps:
"Where shall I find Him? Where shall I go? With whom?"*
verses_en.orig:
ক্ষেণে উচ্চ-স্বরে গায় কারে পহুঁ কি সুধায়
কোথায় আমার প্রাণনাথ ।
ক্ষেণে শীতে অঙ্গ কম্প ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে দেই লম্ফ
কাঁহা পাঙ যাঙ কার সাথ ॥
verses_en.translit:
kṣeṇe ucca-svare gāya kāre pahum̐ ki sudhāya
kothāya āmāra prāṇanātha |
kṣeṇe śīte aṅga kampa kṣeṇe kṣeṇe dei lampha
kām̐hā pāṅa yāṅa kāra sātha ||
verses_en.wbw: kshene uccha-svare gaya — now sings aloud; kare pahun ki sudhaya — whom, what does the Lord ask; kothaya amara prananatha — where is the Lord of my life; kshene shite anga kampa — now the body trembles as with cold; kshene kshene dei lampha — now He leaps; kanha pana — where shall I find; yana kara satha — where go, with whom
notes: Radha's words in separation: She seeks Krishna and does not know where to go. Trembling is a sattvika-bhava; in PK

verses_en.text:
Now, raising His arms, He dances, whirling and whirling,
now again and again He speaks incoherently;
now He closes His eyes and weeps, "O Natha!",
now again and again He is in torment.
verses_en.orig:
ক্ষেণে ঊর্দ্ধবাহু করি নাচি বুলে ফিরি ফিরি
ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে করয়ে প্রলাপ ।
ক্ষেণে আঁখিযুগ মুন্দে হা নাথ বলিয়া কান্দে
ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে করয়ে সন্তাপ ॥
verses_en.translit:
kṣeṇe ūrddhabāhu kari nāci bule phiri phiri
kṣeṇe kṣeṇe karaye pralāpa |
kṣeṇe ām̐khiyuga munde hā nātha baliyā kānde
kṣeṇe kṣeṇe karaye santāpa ||
verses_en.wbw: kshene urdhva-bahu kari — now raising His arms; nachi bule phiri phiri — dances whirling round and round; kshene kshene karaye pralapa — now again and again speaks incoherently; kshene ankhiyuga munde — now closes His eyes; ha natha boliya kande — weeps crying "O Natha!"; kshene kshene karaye santapa — now again and again is in torment

verses_en.text: Narahari Dasa says: ah, my Gaurahari
verses_en.orig:
কহে দাস নরহরি আরে মোর গৌরহরি
রাধার পিরিতে হৈল হেন ।
ঐছন করিয়া চিতে কলিযুগ উদ্ধারিতে
বঞ্চিত হইলুঁ মুঞি কেন ॥
verses_en.translit:
kahe dāsa narahari āre mora gaurahari
rādhāra pirite haila hena |
aichana kariyā cite kaliyuga uddhārite
bañcita hailum̐ muñi kena ||
verses_en.wbw: kahe dasa narahari — Narahari Dasa says; are mora gaurahari — ah, my Gaurahari; radhara pirite haila hena — became thus through Radha's love; aichhana kariya chite — so resolving in His heart; kaliyuga uddharite — to deliver the age of Kali; banchita hailun muni kena — why am I left out

padas.ref: Без подписи (ГПТ — Васу Гхош; рук. П-Р-Са — Говинда Дас), ПК 1663 «চেতন পাইয়া গোরা রায়»
padas.title: Придя в себя у моря: «Где Мой Кришна с флейтой?»
padas.summary: Придя в чувство, Гора озирается, видит Сварупу и Рамарая и восклицает: «Где Мой Кришна с флейтой? Я только что видел Его! О Владыка, яви Себя!»; преданные плачут.

verses.text:
Придя в чувство, Гора Рай,
лёжа на земле, озирается вокруг.
verses.orig:
চেতন পাইয়া গোরা রায় ।
ভূমে পড়ি ইতি উতি চায় ॥
verses.translit:
cetana pāiyā gorā rāya |
bhūme paṛi iti uti cāya ||
verses.wbw: четана пайя — придя в чувство; гора рая — Гора Рай; бхуме пари — лёжа на земле; ити ути чая — озирается вокруг

verses.text:
Перед Ним — Сварупа и Рамарай;
видя их, Господь восклицает: «Увы, увы!
verses.orig:
সম্মুখে স্বরূপ রাম রায় ।
দেখি পহুঁ করে হায় হায় ॥
verses.translit:
sammukhe svarūpa rāma rāya |
dekhi pahum̐ kare hāya hāya ||
verses.wbw: саммукхе — перед [Ним]; сварупа рама рая — Сварупа [и] Рамарай; декхи — видя [их]; паху каре хая хая — Господь восклицает: «Увы, увы!»

verses.text:
Где Мой Кришна с флейтой у уст?
Я только что видел Его!
verses.orig:
কাঁহা মোর মুরলী-বদন ।
এখনি পাইলুঁ দরশন ॥
verses.translit:
kām̐hā mora muralī-badana |
ekhani pāilum̐ daraśana ||
verses.wbw: канха мора мурали-бадана — где мой [Кришна] с флейтой у уст; экхани пайлун дарашана — только что я видел [Его]

verses.text:
О Владыка, безмерно милостивый,
смилуйся, яви Себя!»*
verses.orig:
ওহে নাথ পরম-করুণ ।
কৃপা করি দেহ দরশন ॥
verses.translit:
ohe nātha parama-karuṇa |
kṛpā kari deha daraśana ||
verses.wbw: охе натха — о Владыка; парама-каруна — безмерно милостивый; крипа кари — смилуйся; деха дарашана — яви Себя
notes: «Кришна с флейтой у уст» — в оригинале «мурали-бадана», «Тот, чьё лицо — с флейтой». Господь говорит в бхаве Радхи,

verses.text: Так сетует Горачанд;
verses.orig:
এত বিলাপয়ে গোরাচান্দে ।
দেখিয়া ভকতগণ কান্দে ॥
verses.translit:
eta bilāpaye gorācānde |
dekhiyā bhakatagaṇa kānde ||
verses.wbw: эта билапайе — так сетует; горачанде — Горачанд; декхия — видя [это]; бхакатагана канде — плачут преданные

verses_en.text:
Coming to His senses, Gora Raya,
lying on the ground, looks this way and that.
verses_en.orig:
চেতন পাইয়া গোরা রায় ।
ভূমে পড়ি ইতি উতি চায় ॥
verses_en.translit:
cetana pāiyā gorā rāya |
bhūme paṛi iti uti cāya ||
verses_en.wbw: chetana paiya — regaining consciousness; gora raya — Gora Raya; bhume pari — lying on the ground; iti uti chaya — looks here and there

verses_en.text:
Before Him are Svarupa and Ramaraya;
seeing them, the Lord cries, "Alas, alas!
verses_en.orig:
সম্মুখে স্বরূপ রাম রায় ।
দেখি পহুঁ করে হায় হায় ॥
verses_en.translit:
sammukhe svarūpa rāma rāya |
dekhi pahum̐ kare hāya hāya ||
verses_en.wbw: sammukhe — in front; svarupa rama raya — Svarupa [and] Ramaraya; dekhi — seeing [them]; pahun kare haya haya — the Lord cries "Alas, alas!"

verses_en.text:
Where is My Krishna with the flute at His lips?
I saw Him just now!
verses_en.orig:
কাঁহা মোর মুরলী-বদন ।
এখনি পাইলুঁ দরশন ॥
verses_en.translit:
kām̐hā mora muralī-badana |
ekhani pāilum̐ daraśana ||
verses_en.wbw: kanha mora murali-badana — where is my flute-faced one; ekhani pailun darashana — just now I had His sight

verses_en.text:
O Lord, supremely merciful,
be gracious, show Yourself!"*
verses_en.orig:
ওহে নাথ পরম-করুণ ।
কৃপা করি দেহ দরশন ॥
verses_en.translit:
ohe nātha parama-karuṇa |
kṛpā kari deha daraśana ||
verses_en.wbw: ohe natha — O Lord; parama-karuna — supremely merciful; kripa kari — be gracious; deha darashana — grant Your sight
notes: "Krishna with the flute at His lips" — in the original "murali-badana", "He whose face bears the flute". The Lord

verses_en.text: So laments Gorachand;
verses_en.orig:
এত বিলাপয়ে গোরাচান্দে ।
দেখিয়া ভকতগণ কান্দে ॥
verses_en.translit:
eta bilāpaye gorācānde |
dekhiyā bhakatagaṇa kānde ||
verses_en.wbw: eta bilapaye — thus laments; gorachande — Gorachand; dekhiya — seeing [this]; bhakatagana kande — the devotees weep

padas.poet: Без подписи (ГПТ — Васу Гхош; рук. П-Р-Са — Говинда Дас)

gaura-stotras.title: Обмороки в разлуке в саду у озера
gaura-stotras.summary: В саду на берегу озера Господь, терзаемый разлукой с Кришной, льёт реки слёз и снова и снова лишается чувств.

verses.text: В саду на берегу озера<sup>*</sup>, терзаемый разлукой с Луной Гокулы, Он потоками слёз из очей творил новую реку, раз за разом лишался чувств — и весь мир делал словно мёртвым<sup>*</sup>. Вновь ли сын Шачи предстанет моим очам?
notes: saras-tīrārāme (по GGM sarottīrārāme; у Пуридаса строка искажена OCR, смысл тот же) — сад на берегу озера; в Пури — вероятно, сады у Нарендра-саровары или Джаганнатха-валлабха. Точное место автор не называет.
Ср. ЧЧ Антья 14–19 — лилы божественного безумия Господа в разлуке с Кришной, очевидцем которых был Рагхунатха.

verses_en.text: In a garden on the shore of a lake<sup>*</sup>, tormented by separation from the Moon of Gokula, He made a new river with the streams of tears from His eyes, swooned again and again — and made the whole world as though dead<sup>*</sup>. Will the son of Shachi come again before my eyes?
notes: saras-tīrārāme (GGM sarottīrārāme; in Puridasa the line is garbled by OCR, the sense being the same) — a garden on a lake shore; in Puri, probably the gardens by the Narendra-sarovara or the Jagannatha-vallabha garden. The author does not name the place.
Cf. CC Antya 14–19 — the pastimes of the Lord's divine madness in separation from Krishna, which Raghunatha witnessed.

gaura-stotras.title: Сады у океана напоминают о Вриндаване
gaura-stotras.summary: На берегу океана, при виде садов, Господь, вспомнив Вриндаван, теряет власть над Собой от любви и непрестанно повторяет «Кришна».

verses.text: На берегу океана, при виде рядов цветущих садов, Он снова и снова теряет власть над Собой от любви, рождённой памятью о Вриндаване; порою язык Его не может остановиться, повторяя «Кришна»; Он — вкушающий расу преданности<sup>*</sup>. Вновь ли тот Чайтанья предстанет моим очам?
notes: Сады на побережье Пури напоминали Господу леса Вриндавана; ср. ЧЧ Мадхья 14 и Антья 14–19.

verses_en.text: On the shore of the ocean, at the sight of rows of flourishing gardens, He is again and again overpowered by love born of the remembrance of Vrindavana; at times His tongue cannot cease repeating "Krishna"; He is the relisher of the rasa of devotion<sup>*</sup>. Will that Chaitanya come again before my eyes?
notes: The gardens on the shore at Puri reminded the Lord of the forests of Vrindavana; cf. CC Madhya 14 and Antya 14–19.

vaishnava-lilamrita.title: Махабхава Прабху: Гамбхира, разлука, море, туча, Тота-Гопинатха
vaishnava-lilamrita.summary: Прабху пребывает в махабхаве в Гамбхире: встаёт, садится, катается по земле с криком «О Кришна!», оставляет счёт имён на поясном шнуре, бежит в храм искать Кришну, к морю — увидеть Его облик, теряет себя при виде тучи; бывает у Тота-Гопинатхи и в Кунджа-матхе.

verses.text:
Сколько у Прабху махабхав — кто сможет их описать?
7.115. Порой Он пребывает в махабхаве — в Гамбхире, на миг (?).*
7.116. Встаёт, садится, катается [по земле], восклицая: «О Кришна!»
7.117. Из очей струятся слёзы — Он исполнен любви к Кришне.
7.118. Эта мука разлуки с Кришной проявилась в теле Прабху.*
7.119. Он оставляет обычай считать имена при джапе на поясном шнуре.*
7.120. В исступлении Он проводит (?) день; как дитя (?), являет [Свою] бхаву.*
7.121. Порой бежит в храм: «Где мой Кришна?» — чтобы увидеть [Его].*
7.122. Восклицая: «О Кришна!», Он громко плачет, а порой хулит Свой облик.*
7.123. Порой бежит к морю, чтобы увидеть облик Кришны.
7.124. Увидев, как в небе поднимается туча, Он приходит в смятение.*
7.125. Порой Он [бывает] у Тота-Гопинатхи, а порой сидит в Кунджа-матхе.*
notes: Гамбхира — маленькая комната в доме Каши Мишры в Пури, где Махапрабху провёл последние годы в глубоких чувствах разлуки (ЧЧ, Антья 14–20). Последнее слово печ. ≈ ଲବେ: labe «на миг» (laba «мгновение») или labhe «обретает»?
Випраламбха — переживание разлуки с Кришной в настроении Радхи. Его изображает почти вся Антья-лила ЧЧ.
Бук. «джапа имени на поясном шнуре — оставляет привычку считать». По-видимому, речь о счёте повторений святого имени узлами на шнуре. В ЧЧ мы этой подробности не нашли.
Mata = matta «опьянённый, в исступлении». Nie (печ. ≈ залитое ନ + ଏ; ନି, как в ନିଜ 7.122) понято как «проводит [день]». Parāẏa (печ. ≈ ପ + ର/ରା + ୟ) понято как prāẏa «подобно».
Деула — храм Джаганнатхи. По ЧЧ, Махапрабху ежедневно ходил на даршан Джаганнатхи и видел в Нём Кришну.
Возможно, в настроении Радхи, тоскующей по Кришне, Он порицает Своё тело. Ср. в ЧЧ (Антья 17–19) речи Махапрабху в разлуке.
Туча напоминает цвет тела Кришны. Ср. ЧЧ (Антья 14, 18): Махапрабху принимает холм Чатака за Говардхану, а море — за Ямуну.

Тота-Гопинатха — Божество Гопинатхи в саду (ṭoṭā) у моря в Пури; Ему служил Гададхара Пандит (ЧЧ, Антья 7), учитель Мадхавы. Напечатано ତୋଟା (обычно ଟୋଟା). Кунджа-матх (kuñjamaṭha) нами не опознан. Первое слово 125а печ. ≈ େକ + искажённая େ + ବ; читаем କେବେ «порой».

verses_en.text:
However many mahabhavas Prabhu has — who could describe them?
7.115. Sometimes He remains in mahabhava — in the Gambhira, for a moment (?).*
7.116. He rises, sits down, rolls [on the ground], crying out, "O Krishna!"
7.117. Tears stream from His eyes — He is full of love for Krishna.
7.118. This torment of separation from Krishna became manifest in Prabhu's body.*
7.119. He gives up the habit of counting the names in japa on a waist-cord.*
7.120. In frenzy He passes (?) the day; like a child (?) He shows [His] bhava.*
7.121. Sometimes He runs to the temple — "Where is my Krishna?" — to see [Him].*
7.122. Crying "O Krishna!", He weeps aloud, and sometimes He reviles His own form.*
7.123. Sometimes He runs to the sea to see the form of Krishna.
7.124. Seeing a cloud rise in the sky, He is overcome with agitation.*
7.125. Sometimes He [is] at Tota-Gopinatha, and sometimes He sits in the Kunja-matha.*
notes: The Gambhira is a small room in Kashi Mishra's house in Puri, where Mahaprabhu spent His last years in deep feelings of separation (CC, Antya 14–20). The last word is printed ≈ ଲବେ: labe "for a moment" (laba "instant") or labhe "attains"?
Vipralambha — the experience of separation from Krishna in the mood of Radha. Almost the entire Antya-lila of the CC depicts it.

Literally, "japa of the name on the waist-cord — He gives up the habit of counting." Apparently this refers to counting repetitions of the holy name with knots on a cord. We have not found this detail in the CC.
Mata = matta "intoxicated, in frenzy." Nie (printed ≈ a filled ନ + ଏ; ନି as in ନିଜ, 7.122) is taken as "passes [the day]." Parāẏa (printed ≈ ପ + ର/ରା + ୟ) is taken as prāẏa "like."
The deula is the temple of Jagannatha. According to the CC, Mahaprabhu went daily for darshan of Jagannatha and saw Krishna in Him.
Perhaps, in the mood of Radha longing for Krishna, He reproaches His own body. Cf. Mahaprabhu's words in separation in the CC (Antya 17–19).
A cloud recalls the color of Krishna's body. Cf. the CC (Antya 14, 18): Mahaprabhu takes the Chataka hill for Govardhana and the sea for the Yamuna.

Tota-Gopinatha is the Deity of Gopinatha in the garden (ṭoṭā) by the sea in Puri; Gadadhara Pandita, Madhava's teacher, served Him (CC, Antya 7). Printed ତୋଟା (usually ଟୋଟା). The Kunja-matha (kuñjamaṭha) has not been identified. The first word of 125a is printed ≈ େକ + a distorted େ + ବ; read as କେବେ "sometimes."

vaishnava-lilamrita.title: Махабхава Прабху (окончание): Гундича, пруды, Свами кормит Его; Панчасакха всегда при Нём
vaishnava-lilamrita.summary: Прабху созерцает облик Кришны в мандапе Гундичи, теряет чувства, катается в пыли, бежит к Нарендре и Маркандее, неистово танцует в киртане, не помнит о сне и еде; Свами насильно кормит Его; рядом со Сварупой Он являет махабхаву; Свами знает Его бхаву и просит отдать ум киртану; Прабху велит Панчасакхе всегда быть при Нём; подпись главы.

verses.text:
А порой Он идёт в Гундичу (?) и, сев в мандапе, [погружается] в созерцание.*
7.127. В уединении, в созерцании облика Кришны, Он размышляет, вкушая бхаву.
7.128. То и дело Он лишается чувств, а порой волоски на Его теле встают дыбом.*
7.129. А порой катается в пыли, вымазав пылью всё тело.
7.130. Бежит к пруду Нарендра, а порой погружается в [пруд] Маркандеи.*
7.131. Упоённый расой киртана, Он неистово (?) танцует.*
7.132. Раскачивается взад и вперёд, с громким кличем совершает прыжки.
7.133. А порой Он пребывает в [обычном] естестве (?) и радостно беседует.*
7.134. Он лишь упоён (?) радостью танца, исполнен любви к расе киртана.*
7.135. Ум Его не [задерживается] на сне и еде — знайте [это].
7.136. Свами приносит блюдо с едой и кормит [Его] насильно (?).*
7.137. Рядом со Сварупой Дамодарой Он являет махабхаву.*
7.138. Видя [это], люди изумлены; понимают ли (?) они состояние Прабху?*
7.139. Сокровище премы Нилачалы — знайте: вот что зовётся «Прабху».*
7.140. Воочию [Он] — воплощение премы; Он — предел расы премы.*
7.141. Никто не знает Его бхавы — эту природу [Его] знает Свами.*
7.142. [Свами] говорит: «Прабху, успокойся, отдай ум расе киртана.
7.143. В киртане — воплощение Твоей бхавы; разве люди поймут (??) [его]?»*
7.144. Баларама и Джаганнатха, Ананта, Ачьюта, Яшованта —*
7.145. эти пятеро, собравшись возле Прабху, ходят, упоённые расой киртана.
7.146. Прабху сказал: «Да будет так (?)! Будь всегда со Мной».*
7.147. Прабху являет бхаву — и называет это человеческой лилой.*
7.148. Так говорит Мадхава-дас, возлагая надежду на стопы Прабху.*
notes: Гундича — храм в Пури, куда на Ратха-ятре отвозят Джаганнатху; мандапа — открытый павильон храма. Пребывание Махапрабху у Гундичи на празднике колесниц описано в ЧЧ (Мадхья 12–14). Последний знак слова guṇḍicā напечатан ≈ ଚ с подстрочным крючком, знака ା не видно; чтение ଗୁଣ୍ଡିଚା восстановлено по рифме с bhābanā.

Первые слова напечатаны ≈ «କ୍ଷଣେ କ୍ଷଣ କେ» (с пробелом) и прочитаны как kṣaṇe kṣaṇake «то и дело, ежеминутно» (ср. kṣaṇake 7.106). Kāẏe «в теле» — мест. п. от kāẏa. Обмороки и вставшие дыбом волоски — саттвика-бхавы, признаки экстатической любви (ЧЧ, Мадхья 2; Антья 14).

Нарендра-саровар и Маркандея-саровар — священные пруды Пури. В ЧЧ Махапрабху с преданными совершает водные игры в Нарендра-сароваре (Мадхья 11 и 14 — проверить); омовение в Маркандее у Мадхавы — подробность, которой в ЧЧ, по-видимому, нет.

Matta «упоённый» напечатано ମ + знак, похожий на ଢ (так же в 7.145); понято как лигатура ତ୍ତ (ср. ମତ в 7.120). Последнее слово напечатано ≈ ପ୍ରବରଳ (так же читает OCR); понято как ପ୍ରବଳ «бурно, неистово».

Prakṛtire — бук. «в природе, в естестве». Понято как «в обычном состоянии», т. е. во внешнем сознании, когда Махапрабху беседует с преданными (ср. три состояния — внутреннее, полувнешнее и внешнее, ЧЧ, Антья 14–20). Возможно и другое понимание: prakṛti — «женская природа», т. е. настроение гопи. Sukhare «радостно» (так и в OCR), а не mukhare «устами».
Слово после ekā tā напечатано ≈ ପ/ସ + тот же знак, что в matta 7.131 (OCR: ସଭ); прочитано как matta «упоённый», хотя первый знак похож скорее на ପ/ସ, чем на ମ.

Свами — Джаганнатха Дас (ср. 7.2). Печатное ≈ ବଲକ୍କାର понято как ବଳାତ୍କାର «силой, насильно». В ЧЧ о еде Махапрабху в годы глубокой разлуки заботятся Сварупа Дамодара, Говинда и Джагадананда (ЧЧ, Антья); Джаганнатха Дас в ЧЧ/ЧБ не упоминается — это орийская традиция Мадхавы.
Сварупа Дамодара — ближайший спутник Махапрабху в Пури в последние годы. По ЧЧ (Антья 14–20), именно ему и Рамананде Раю Господь открывал Свои чувства разлуки в Гамбхире.

Udanta — «весть, история, обстоятельства», здесь — состояние Прабху. Глагол напечатан ≈ ବୁ + ଝ со штрихом над ним + ନ୍ତ (‑ି не видна; так же в 7.143); прочитан как bujhanti «понимают». Возможно и утвердительное понимание: «люди… постигают состояние Прабху».
Синтаксис 7.139б («ପ୍ରଭୁ ଏ ବୋଲିବାଟି ଜାଣ») понят так: «знай: это — то, что называют „Прабху“». Bolibāṭi напечатано ≈ ବୋଲବାଟି (‑ି утрачена). Ср. провозглашение Чайтаньи «Прабху» в 7.112.
Pratimā (печ. ≈ ପ୍ରତମା) здесь — «воплощение, подобие» премы, а не Божество в храме.

У Мадхавы Свами (Джаганнатха Дас) один знает бхаву Прабху, успокаивает Его и обращается к Нему на «ты» (tora, 7.143). По ЧЧ (Антья 14–20), внутреннее настроение Махапрабху понимал Сварупа Дамодара, который утешал Его песнями и стихами, созвучными Его чувствам; гаудия-вайшнавы, вслед за Шрилой Бхактисиддхантой Сарасвати, следуют этому описанию. Что говорит Свами (а не Прабху), понято по смыслу (ср. 7.141б); говорящий в 7.142а не обозначен.

Слово после manuṣya напечатано ≈ ଭ без черты лигатуры ଭା + ର (OCR неразборчив). Прочитано как bhara (??) — смысл неясен («полноту [бхавы]»?); возможно, опечатка вместо ଭାବ «состояние». Переведено по общему смыслу.
Панчасакха — Баларама Дас, Джаганнатха Дас, Ананта, Ачьюта (Ачьютананда) и Яшованта (ср. 7.102, 8.4). Двустишие синтаксически продолжается в 7.145. Cāli «ходят, двигаются» (7.145б) — оттенок неясен.

Слово 7.146а напечатано ≈ ଅ + ସ с подстрочным знаком (ତ/ଥ) и ୁ (OCR: ଅସ୍ତ); прочитано как astu «да будет так». Āmbha tule — «с Нами», почтит. «со Мной». Кому обращено ед. ч. tu «ты» (при пятерых спутниках в 7.145), неясно — возможно, Свами.

Подлежащее bolaï «называет» понято как Прабху: Он являет бхаву, но называет это человеческой лилой. Ср. ЧЧ (Мадхья 21): из всех игр Кришны высшая — нара-лила, игры в человеческом облике; Махапрабху, скрывая Свою божественность, действует как преданный.
Заключительная формула с именем автора (ср. 2.131). Этим стихом глава 7 кончается: после него — орнаментальный знак, колофона «ଇତି… ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ» нет; глава 8 («ଅଷ୍ଟମ ଅଧ୍ୟାୟ») начинается на листе 105.

verses_en.text:
And at times He goes to Gundicha (?) and, sitting in the mandapa, [becomes absorbed] in contemplation.*
7.127. In solitude, meditating on Krishna's form, He ponders, relishing bhava.
7.128. Again and again He faints, and at times the hairs of His body stand on end.*
7.129. And at times He rolls in the dust, smearing His whole body with dust.
7.130. He runs to the Narendra tank, and at times plunges into the Markandeya [tank].*
7.131. Intoxicated with the rasa of kirtana, He dances wildly (?).*
7.132. He sways back and forth, and with loud cries makes leaps.
7.133. And at times He abides in [His ordinary] nature (?) and converses joyfully.*
7.134. He is solely intoxicated (?) with the joy of dance, full of love for the rasa of kirtana.*
7.135. His mind does not [rest] on sleep or food — know [this].
7.136. The Swami brings a plate of food and makes [Him] eat by force (?).*
7.137. Beside Svarupa Damodara He reveals mahabhava.*
7.138. Seeing [this], people are astonished; do (?) they understand Prabhu's state?*
7.139. The treasure of prema of Nilachala — know: this is what is called "Prabhu."*
7.140. Manifestly [He] is the embodiment of prema; He is the utmost limit of the rasa of prema.*
7.141. No one knows His bhava — this nature [of His] the Swami knows.*
7.142. [The Swami] says: "Prabhu, be calm; give Your mind to the rasa of kirtana.
7.143. In kirtana is the embodiment of Your bhava; how can people understand (??) [it]?"*
7.144. Balarama and Jagannatha, Ananta, Achyuta, Yashovanta —*
7.145. these five, gathering beside Prabhu, go about intoxicated with the rasa of kirtana.
7.146. Prabhu said: "So be it (?)! Stay always with Me."*
7.147. Prabhu manifests bhava — and calls it a human lila.*
7.148. So says Madhava-dasa, placing his hope in Prabhu's feet.*
notes: Gundicha is the temple in Puri to which Jagannatha is drawn at the Ratha-yatra; the mandapa is the temple's open pavilion. Mahaprabhu's stay at Gundicha during the chariot festival is described in CC, Madhya 12–14. The last sign of guṇḍicā is printed ≈ ଚ with a subscript hook, with no visible ା; the reading ଗୁଣ୍ଡିଚା is restored from the rhyme with bhābanā.

The first words are printed ≈ "କ୍ଷଣେ କ୍ଷଣ କେ" (with a gap) and read as kṣaṇe kṣaṇake "again and again, every moment" (cf. kṣaṇake 7.106). Kāẏe "in the body" is the locative of kāẏa. Fainting and hair standing on end are sattvika-bhavas, signs of ecstatic love (CC, Madhya 2; Antya 14).

Narendra-sarovara and Markandeya-sarovara are sacred tanks of Puri. In the CC Mahaprabhu and the devotees perform water pastimes in Narendra-sarovara (Madhya 11 and 14 — to be checked); the bath in the Markandeya tank is a detail of Madhava's that apparently does not appear in the CC.

Matta "intoxicated" is printed ମ + a sign like ଢ (likewise in 7.145); taken as the ligature ତ୍ତ (cf. ମତ in 7.120). The last word is printed ≈ ପ୍ରବରଳ (so also the OCR); taken as ପ୍ରବଳ "vehemently, wildly."

Prakṛtire — lit. "in nature, in [one's own] state." Taken as "in the ordinary state," i.e. in external consciousness, when Mahaprabhu converses with the devotees (cf. the three states — internal, half-external and external, CC, Antya 14–20). Another understanding is possible: prakṛti as "feminine nature," i.e. the mood of a gopi. Sukhare "joyfully" (so also the OCR), not mukhare "with the mouth."
The word after ekā tā is printed ≈ ପ/ସ + the same sign as in matta 7.131 (OCR: ସଭ); read as matta "intoxicated," although the first sign looks more like ପ/ସ than ମ.

The Swami is Jagannatha Dasa (cf. 7.2). The printed ≈ ବଲକ୍କାର is taken as ବଳାତ୍କାର "by force." In the CC, Svarupa Damodara, Govinda and Jagadananda look after Mahaprabhu's meals in the years of deep separation (CC, Antya); Jagannatha Dasa is not mentioned in the CC/CB — this is Madhava's Odia tradition.

Svarupa Damodara was Mahaprabhu's closest companion in Puri in the last years. According to the CC (Antya 14–20), it was to him and Ramananda Raya that the Lord disclosed His feelings of separation in the Gambhira.

Udanta — "tidings, account, circumstances," here Prabhu's state. The verb is printed ≈ ବୁ + ଝ with a stroke above + ନ୍ତ (‑i not visible; likewise in 7.143); read as bujhanti "understand." An affirmative understanding is also possible: "people… grasp Prabhu's state."
The syntax of 7.139b ("ପ୍ରଭୁ ଏ ବୋଲିବାଟି ଜାଣ") is taken as "know: this is what is called 'Prabhu'." Bolibāṭi is printed ≈ ବୋଲବାଟି (‑i lost). Cf. the proclamation of Chaitanya as "Prabhu" in 7.112.
Pratimā (printed ≈ ପ୍ରତମା) here means the "embodiment, likeness" of prema, not a temple Deity.

In Madhava, the Swami (Jagannatha Dasa) alone knows Prabhu's bhava, calms Him and addresses Him with the familiar "you" (tora, 7.143). According to the CC (Antya 14–20), it was Svarupa Damodara who understood Mahaprabhu's inner mood and consoled Him with songs and verses in tune with His feelings; Gaudiya Vaishnavas, following Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, follow this account. That the Swami (and not Prabhu) is speaking is inferred from the sense (cf. 7.141b); the speaker of 7.142a is not marked.

The word after manuṣya is printed ≈ ଭ without the stroke of the ligature ଭା + ର (OCR illegible). Read as bhara (??) — meaning unclear ("the fullness [of bhava]"?); possibly a misprint for ଭାବ "state." Translated by the general sense.

The Panchasakha are Balarama Dasa, Jagannatha Dasa, Ananta, Achyuta (Achyutananda) and Yashovanta (cf. 7.102, 8.4). The couplet continues syntactically in 7.145. Cāli "go about, move" (7.145b) — the nuance is unclear.

The word in 7.146a is printed ≈ ଅ + ସ with a subscript sign (ତ/ଥ) and ୁ (OCR: ଅସ୍ତ); read as astu "so be it." Āmbha tule — "with Us," honorific "with Me." To whom the singular tu "you" is addressed (with five companions in 7.145) is unclear — perhaps the Swami.

The subject of bolaï "calls" is taken to be Prabhu: He manifests bhava but calls it a human lila. Cf. CC, Madhya 21: of all Krishna's pastimes the highest is nara-lila, the pastimes in human form; Mahaprabhu, concealing His divinity, acts as a devotee.

The closing formula with the author's name (cf. 2.131). With this verse Chapter 7 ends: it is followed by an ornament, with no colophon "ଇତି… ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ"; Chapter 8 ("ଅଷ୍ଟମ ଅଧ୍ୟାୟ") begins on leaf 105.

nityananda-vamsha.title: Господь погружён в бхаву Радхи и разлуку с Кришной; вкушает её со Сварупой
nityananda-vamsha.summary: С того дня Господь день и ночь говорит языком разлуки с Кришной в настроении Радхи, вкушая эту расу лишь со Сварупой Дамодарой и хранящий санкиртану имени как дхарму века; сокровенный замысел, открытый Нитьянанде, Он лишь намёком раскрывает самым близким.

verses.text:
Утром оба Прабху, совершив ежедневные обряды,
пошли и, не мигая, смотрели на красоту Джаганнатхи.

С того дня какое же состояние охватило Прабху!
Без конца он говорил языком разлуки с Кришной.

День и ночь, погружённый в чувства Радхи,
он вкушал всю горечь разлуки с Кришной.

Вкушал достоинства Радхи только вместе со Сварупой*;
этой расы не знает никто, кроме самых близких преданных.
notes: Сварупа Дамодара — ближайший спутник Чайтаньи в Пури, с которым тот делился переживаниями в настроении Радхи.

verses.text:
Хранить дхарму века — санкиртану имени Кришны:
в этих двух расах был погружён Шри Шачинандана*.
notes: Шачинандана — «сын Шачи», Чайтанья.

verses.text:
Вкушая расу чувства и расу имени,
он сам поступал так и тем учил людей мира.

Все сокровенные беседы, что были у него с Нитьянандой,
он раскрыл в их сути лишь самым близким преданным.

Эту глубочайшую тайну не узнал никто;
весь замысел Прабху понял только Прабху (Нитьянанда).
Намёком он поведал её близким преданным;

verses_en.text:
In the morning the two Lords, having performed their daily rites,
went and gazed unblinking at the beauty of Jagannatha.

From that day, what a state came over the Lord!
Ceaselessly he spoke the language of separation from Krishna.

Day and night, absorbed in Radha's mood,
he tasted all the pain of separation from Krishna.

He tasted Radha's virtues with Svarupa alone;*
none but the most intimate devotees know this rasa.
notes: Svarupa Damodara, Chaitanya's closest companion in Puri, with whom he shared his experiences in Radha's mood.

verses_en.text:
Upholding the dharma of the age, the sankirtana of Krishna's name —
in these two rasas Sri Shachinandana was immersed.*
notes: Shachinandana, "the son of Shachi", i.e. Chaitanya.

verses_en.text:
Tasting the rasa of feeling and the rasa of the name,
he practised it himself and so taught the people of the world.

All the secret talks he had had with Nityananda
he revealed in their essence only to his intimate devotees.

No one learnt this deepest secret;
only the Lord (Nityananda) understood the whole of the Lord's mind.
By hints he told it to his intimate devotees;

advaita-prakasha.title: Господь отсылает преданных проповедовать, велит Нитьянанде жениться и уходит в уединение с именем
advaita-prakasha.summary: После праздника Господь говорит преданным, что им незачем снова приходить: пусть на родине раздают имя; Он велит Нитьянанде жениться, а Сам уходит в сокровенное место, непрестанно повторяя имя Хари: «Что имя, то и Хари — нет никакого различия».

verses.text: После праздника колесниц Гаура созвал преданных и сказал: «Вы много натерпелись из-за Меня.
Не нужно снова и снова приходить сюда: оставайтесь на родине и всегда раздавайте имя.
Вы все родились, чтобы проповедовать вечную дхарму: проповедуя дхарму, сделайте жизнь плодотворной.
Несколько дней Я проведу в сокровенном месте — тогда исполнятся все Мои желания».
Он велел Нитьянанде жениться, и по повелению Гауры преданные разошлись по своим краям.
Войдя в сокровенное место, Гора, погружённый в любовь, непрестанно повторял имя Хари.
Видя любимых преданных, Он говорил: «Суть всего — имя Хари: без имени Хари у души нет иного пути.
Пойте имя, думайте об имени, сделайте имя сутью: вместе с именем играет Хари.
Что имя, то и Хари — нет никакого различия: это с доказательствами говорят Пураны и Веды».

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Sri Rupa saw in a dream Mahaprabhu speaking gently to him:
"Hey, Rupa, you have conceived a wondrous play and revealed in it the divine pastimes of Radha and Shyama.
I have a great longing to hear that sweet and beautiful play."
Having said this, Sri Chaitanya vanished, and Rupa, waking, fainted in the ecstasy of love.
After some time the king of devotees came to himself and wept: "Where is Gauranga?"
Now he said: "Your divine pastimes are hard to understand: You have descended to exalt the honour of the devotees.
Mercy awoke in You to appear to Your devotee — that is why You came in a dream and gave me a command."
Having said this, Rupa danced wildly. At that time Gosani Sanatana came there.
He said: "Tell me the good news, Rupa: it seems that today Gora has poured out His love."
Rupa replied: "Master, you know all the shastras: in a dream Gora let me know that He wishes to see me."
Sanatana said: "The good fortune of millions of your lives has dawned: you have seen Gauranga — and you will surely see the Lord."
Sri Rupa replied: "Your command is like the Veda. I shall go to Sri Purushottama to see Gauranga."
Having said this, he prostrated himself before Sanatana and, remembering Gaura Hari, set out auspiciously.
In the ecstasy of love for Gaura he came to Sri Kshetra; seeing Gauranga, he shed streams of love from his eyes.
He prostrated himself a hundred times with the eight limbs of his body at Chaitanya's feet, and Gora embraced Sri Rupa tightly.
Rupa said: "I am an untouchable sinner. Why do You make me an offender by touching me?"
Mahaprabhu replied: "You are the best of bhagavatas: your body is like the heavenly Ganga, the Mandakini."
Sri Rupa said: "You are an ocean of mercy: a particle of Your mercy is a mine of every blessing.
Whoever by good fortune touches even a drop of the nectar of Your feet obtains the most pure body of a Sri Vaishnava —
as the water of a well, by the touch of a shalagrama, becomes holy, inaccessible even to the gods and destructive of all sins."
Mahaprabhu said: "This is excessive praise." Rupa replied: "There is not a drop of praise in it."
Then Gora Himself told Raya Ramananda and the others of Rupa's pure detachment.
In Rupa's company the bliss of Gaura's companions increased, and Sri Gauranga began the sankirtana.
In great bliss some sang, others danced, others, intoxicated with love, wept: "Gora!"
At this the waves of the ocean of Gaura's love rose, and He, crying "Hare Krishna," began to dance.
Now joy, now stupor, now sweating, now weeping: "Lord of My life!"
Thus Sri Krishna Chaitanya with the devotees made the world fortunate with a cloud of the nectar of love.
After some time, ending the sankirtana of Hari, all, with Gaura's permission, went about their own affairs.
One day Sri Gauranga was sitting joyfully with the devotees, conversing on holy topics.
At that time Sri Rupa Gosani came there and prostrated himself before Gorachand with the eight limbs of his body.
Gora embraced him and told him to sit down; he, bowing to the devotees, sat at a distance.
The all-knowing Sri Chaitanya, the great Lord, knowing his heart, said to Sri Rupa:
"I have heard from the lips of sadhus that you have composed a play on the pastimes of Sri Krishna.
Read it among the Sri Vaishnavas — I am eager to hear it."
Rupa said: "Where am I — low, the lowest of men — and where are the pastimes of Krishna, higher than all!
As a wingless bird has no power to fly, so this fool has no ability to spread scriptures.
What I have written is like a child's game: I am both ashamed and afraid to reveal it.
But I cannot transgress a command from Your holy lips: forgive, all of you, my offence out of mercy."
Having said this, Rupa read the play; hearing it, all the devotees were filled with the jubilation of love.
Ramaraya and the others, immersed in love, said: "By hearing this play we have been purified.
Such sweet glory of the name of Krishna, such majesty of verse we have never heard anywhere."
Mahaprabhu in the bliss of love said to Sri Rupa: "It would be good to divide this play into two parts:
Vidagdha-Madhava and Lalita-Madhava — under these two names they will be a festival for the heart."
Hearing this, the Sri Vaishnavas cried out the name of Hari, and under these two names the plays became famous throughout the world.
By the inconceivable mercy of Sri Gauranga and His companions the drum of Sri Rupa's fame resounded everywhere.
There was no limit to the humility of Rupa Gosvami; Gauranga and His companions were lost in the bliss of love.
Sri Rupa lived there for several days; by seeing Jagannatha his jubilation of love increased.
Then Mahaprabhu gave him a command, and he, placing it on his head, set out for Vraja.
Neither the Four-faced One nor the others can find the limit of the glory of Sri Gauranga and His devotees.
Hearing it from the lips of sadhus, the mind finds no rest; therefore I speak only briefly, enumerating the essence.
One day Mahaprabhu expounded to Achyuta a commentary on the Bhagavata full of devotion.
Sri Achyuta said: "This commentary is the best of all: there is no need for the commentary of Svami or any other.
It is the essence of all commentaries, and its explanation is fuller." Hearing this, Sri Krishna Chaitanya said to Achyuta:
"That which diminishes the glory of many sadhus — conceal it, obeying My command."
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta said with wonder in his heart: "At such a command my heart breaks.
This commentary of Yours is the sovereign of the kingdom of devotion: in every word of the verse is a treasury of rasa.
By forbidding the spread of such a commentary on devotion You have today shown the truth of the name 'Ocean of Mercy.'"
Having said this, he wept in the bliss of love, and Gora sprinkled him with tears of love.
Ah, the mercy of Sri Chaitanya is a boundless ocean: neither Sri Ananta nor the others find its limit.
Setting aside His own dignity, Gora gives happiness to the souls; such humility Krishna never showed.
Earlier, when Gora was studying the shastras, He composed a commentary on logic.
He was carrying that commentary across the Ganga, and then a brahmana asked Him:
"Venerable sir, what book have you under your arm?" Sri Gauranga replied: "This is a commentary on nyaya."
Looking at the commentary, the brahmana cried out: "My labour has turned to dust!
Seeing this, people will disregard my commentary." Sri Gauranga said: "Do not fear, best of brahmanas."
That very moment mercy awoke in the ocean of mercy, and He threw His own commentary into the Ganga.
Seeing this, that brahmana said in great joy: "No soul could make such a renunciation.
You are surely Vishnu Himself come down to earth: to Your feet my millions of obeisances."
Having said this, the brahmana went away joyfully, and the moonlight of Gorachand's fame filled the world.
Know that the song of Sri Chaitanya's pastimes is inconceivable — I, a worm, enumerate only specks of their essence.
Then Shachinandana said to Sri Achyuta: "Why does My right eye twitch?"
Sri Achyuta replied: "You are auspiciousness itself: all auspicious signs ever abide in You.
Surely the good fortune of some dear devotee is about to dawn — that is why the eye of Him who is subject to His devotees twitches."
At that time Sanatana, the best of bhagavatas, came from Vraja and stood before Gaura.
Seeing him, Sri Gauranga said in the bliss of love: "The word of an eternal devotee of Krishna surely comes true."
Sri Achyuta said: "You are the ruler of the mind: abiding in name and form, You are the doer in the souls."
Hearing this, Mahaprabhu remembered Sri Vishnu, and Sanatana, seeing Gaura, was filled with love.
Seized by stupor, sweating, thrills and the rest, he washed Gaura's feet with tears of love.
Opening His arms, Gora embraced him. He said: "You have made me a great offender.
Not only am I a low untouchable, but my body is also covered with festering sores that arouse disgust."
Mahaprabhu said: "Where are your sores? I see a most pure body, shining like the sun."
Hearing this, Sanatana examined his body and, seeing that he was healthy, was amazed at heart.
Recognizing the inconceivable mercy of Krishna Chaitanya, he raised his arms and began to dance with love.
All the devotees thundered joyfully, and Mahaprabhu began the sankirtana of the Name.
Some played the khol drum, some the karatalas, some laughed and wept with love like those intoxicated.
The waves of the ocean of sankirtana rose ever higher, and Sri Gauranga, in the ecstasy of love, sank into it.
Now tears, now trembling, now unconsciousness; now, crying "Hari," He wept, now He was humble.
After a long time, ending the sankirtana of the Name, Gora sat down in His place with the devotees.
Then Sanatana gently asked Gaura: "Which of the dharmas is called the eternal dharma (sanatana-dharma)?"
Mahaprabhu replied: "You are the best of bhagavatas, versed in all the shastras, discerning in everything.
And yet you have asked, as befits a gentleman: in conversations with the righteous the desire of a sadhu is never satiated.
I call the dharma of the Sri Vaishnavas the eternal dharma; everything else is like secondary dharmas.
The dharma of the Sri Vaishnavas is eternally perfect, say the Vedas; the secondary dharmas Shiva preached at Krishna's command.
Shiva's command is not fruitless — it accomplishes secondary aims; but, as for one who goes by a roundabout way, the labour is multiplied.
By the fruit of worshipping other gods through many lives, when the mind is purified, one obtains the mantra of Vishnu.
Vishnu, like a wish-fulfilling tree, at the desire of His devotee bestows even the rare liberation and the rest."
Sanatana said: "I have understood the gross essence: the dharma of the Sri Vaishnavas is beginningless and perfect."
Mahaprabhu said: "In the best, Vaishnava dharma the chief thing, say the sadhus, is taste for the name of Hari."
Thus He revealed many truths of devotion, and Sanatana and the other devotees rejoiced greatly.
Then, for the chariot festival of Sriman Jagannatha, pilgrims from various lands gathered together.
From the land of Gauda came pilgrims — the companions of Mahaprabhu: Nityananda, Sri Advaita and the other devotees.
Having found His own, Gora rejoiced and in turn asked all the devotees about their welfare.
All, bowing to Gaura, said that all was well, and Sri Chaitanya embraced each one in turn.
Then Mahaprabhu with all the devotees joyfully bathed in the ocean, the king of holy waters.
Together with them He beheld Jagannatha, and all together partook of the maha-prasada.
What bliss there was then cannot be told: only one fortunate in millions of lives sees it.
Then Mahaprabhu spoke and the devotees listened: He described the excellence of the mood of the gopis of Vraja.
Hearing this, the devotees became intoxicated with pure love and together with Gaura began a great sankirtana.
Many groups played khols and karatalas; raising their arms, they danced sweetly.
Advaita, beautiful in dance, was placed in front; in the middle, dancing, went Gaura and Nityananda.
Behind danced the devotees, their hair standing on end, intoxicated with love, in many movements.
The dance was wondrous, to the amazement of the people: surpassing the Gandharvas, all sang the qualities of Hari.
The chakora birds — the devotees — drank the nectar of the sankirtana: some wept in the ecstasy of love, others embraced one another.
Some, intoxicated with feeling, laughed loudly; others in a great ecstasy of love fell unconscious.
The wondrous bliss of the kirtana drew the gods; how many sinners crossed over in the boat of the Name!
On the day of the chariot festival there was the greatest festival — I have no power to describe even a small part of it.
In front went the chariot of Mother Subhadra, behind went the chariot of Balarama.
The chariot of Jagannatha was pulled by hundreds of thousands of people — and they could not move even one corner of it.
All the pilgrims were amazed. Mahaprabhu, smiling, bent down and pulled.
At His mere touch the chariot rolled swiftly, and all the people in great bliss cried out the name of Hari.
Wondrous pastimes does Jagannatha Hari perform: whoever sees Him crosses the ocean of existence.
However one imagines the form of Jagannatha, Hari mercifully shows him that form:
some see the form of Krishna, others Vamana; the Vedas say that such a person is not born again.
But if someone under the sway of maya thinks of worldly things, that alone he sees, and he cannot see Krishna.
There is no limit to the divine pastimes of Sri Jagannatha; the power of the maha-prasada is inaccessible even to the gods.
Rice brought by a chandala is eaten even by a brahmana; whoever doubts it contracts a great disease — such is the truth.
If even a dog eats Sri maha-prasada, the prasada from its mouth is fit food for the gods.
The virtue of maha-prasada is inconceivable and inexhaustible: Sri Ananta and the others do not know its end.
Whoever eats even a particle of maha-prasada is freed from all sins and goes to Sri Vaikuntha.
Such glory of prasada as at Sri Purushottama has been heard of nowhere else.
I am an insignificant worm, I have no power: I have written down only a speck of the essence.
After the chariot festival Gaura called the devotees together and said: "You have suffered much for My sake.
There is no need to come here again and again: remain in your homeland and always distribute the Name.
You were all born to preach the eternal dharma: by preaching dharma, make your lives fruitful.
For some days I shall stay in a secluded place — then all My desires will be fulfilled."
He told Nityananda to marry, and at Gaura's command the devotees returned to their lands.
Entering the secluded place, Gora, immersed in love, ceaselessly chanted the name of Hari.
Seeing His dear devotees, He would say: "The essence of all is the name of Hari: without the name of Hari the soul has no other way.
Sing the Name, think of the Name, make the Name your essence: together with the Name Hari sports.
What the Name is, that is Hari — there is no difference whatever: this the Puranas and the Vedas declare with proof."
Now hear of the disappearance of Brahma-Haridasa, who every day chanted three hundred thousand Names.
Such taste for the name of Hari I have never seen elsewhere: he amazed all the devotees.
Knowing in his heart that his departure had come, Haridasa came into the midst of the sankirtana and lay down.
He pressed Mahaprabhu's lotus feet to his heart and, with the words "Sri Krishna Chaitanya," left his body.
Seeing this, Sri Gauranga cried out loudly (the name of Hari), and the devotees said: "He is the crown of sadhus."
On all sides the wind of the name of Sri Hari rose, and the waves of the sankirtana began to swell.
Sri Chaitanya sank into the ocean of the bliss of love, and all the devotees swam in it.
Then Gora placed Haridasa in samadhi and joyfully held a great festival.
Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is an ocean of mercy: so merciful an incarnation has never been heard of.
Gora is the source of all incarnations, all-powerful; for the deliverance of people — this is the reason for these pastimes.
Pure love and the name of Hari, hard to attain even for Brahma, He mercifully distributed, offering them Himself, without regard to place.
To the feet of Sri Guru and Gauranga my millions of obeisances: I ceaselessly pray for a particle of their mercy.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

advaita-prakasha.title: Божественное безумие Радхи в Господе
advaita-prakasha.summary: В Господе пробуждается божественное безумие Шри Радхи: «Ах, Владыка! Ах, Кришна!» — Он рыдает, не различая дня и ночи, и преданные исполнены страха.

verses.text: В Нём пробудилось божественное безумие Шри Радхи: «Ах, Владыка! Ах, Кришна!» — рыдал Он.
В экстазе махабхавы Он не различал дня и ночи, и в сердцах преданных поселился страх.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Mahaprabhu, sitting in seclusion, said to His most beloved Sri Jagadananda:
"Go quickly to the land of Gauda; first go to Nadia, the place where I was born.
Convey to My mother's feet My millions of obeisances: wherever I may be, I am her servant.
Being a son, I have not been able to fulfil a son's duty, and therefore I am a great offender at her feet.
Even in millions of yugas I cannot repay My debt to her — unless she forgives My offence by her nectarean mercy.
Then I shall be saved; otherwise I shall fall. I take shelter at her holy lotus feet.
Convey My message to the devotees of Krishna, and especially tell the Acharya."
Receiving Mahaprabhu's command, Sri Jagadananda bowed to Gaurachandra and set out for Gauda.
In due course he arrived in Navadvipa and, coming to the feet of Mother Shachi, prostrated himself.
He conveyed the humble words of Sri Gauranga, and hearing them, Shachi blessed Him again and again.
Sri Jagadananda, the necklace on the neck of Gaura's devotees, served Mother Shachi in many ways.
He gave the devotees the news of Sri Gauranga, and hearing it, the pure devotees became mad with love.
Some said: "Ah, Gauranga, why did You become a sannyasi? Having given us the shade of Your feet, why have You plunged us into grief?"
Others said: "My great good fortune has dawned: out of mercy Gora, my life, has remembered me."
Saddened by the devotees' grief, the pandit went to Shantipura and bowed at the Lord's feet.
The Lord embraced him tightly with love and quickly gave him the best seat.
Filled with love, He asked about Gauranga's welfare, and the pandit told in detail the truth about Gaura:
"Now Sri Krishna Chaitanya is always in the divine madness of love: now, crying 'Radha, Radha!', He grieves,
now with a roar He calls: 'Where is the Lord of My life?' — at that cry the heart of every living being melts."
Hearing this, my Lord became mad with pure love: "Ah, Lord!" — without Gauranga He had no other words.
After a watch the Lord became stunned, and in the second watch He roared loudly.
Now He laughed loudly, now He wept, uttering only: "Appearance and disappearance."
Thus many moods arose in Him — I, unworthy, have no power to describe them.
What I see, that I write, not understanding the meaning — as a parrot sings a song because it has been taught.
Then the Lord honoured the pandit lavishly, and they spent the night talking of Gaura's qualities.
In the morning Jagadananda humbly asked Sri Advaita's leave to go.
The Lord spoke in hints a riddle (tarja) which no one but Gaura can understand.
The Lord said: "Sri Gauranga is the treasure of My life. Convey this to His crimson holy feet:
tell the Baul: 'People have become bauls (madmen)'; tell the Baul: 'Rice no longer sells in the market';
tell the Baul: 'There is no more need for the work'; tell the Baul: 'This is said by a baul.'"
Hearing this, Sri Jagadananda smiled slightly and, having pleased the Lord, set out for Nilachala.
After some days he arrived at Sri Kshetra; seeing Gaura, he shed streams of love from both eyes.
He prostrated himself before Sri Chaitanya with the eight limbs of his body, and He rose and embraced Sri Jagadananda.
Then, joining his palms, the pandit related in order: "The devotees of Nadia are well.
Incomparable is the motherly love of Mother Shachi: for Your welfare she prays to the gods.
She begs blessings for You from the sadhus and, raising her arms, blesses You herself.
What more can I say of Mother Vishnupriya? Seeing her devotion and fidelity, I was amazed.
She serves Mother Shachi in many ways — a thousand people could not serve like that.
Every day at dawn she goes with Mother Shachi to bathe in the Ganga and returns home.
And after that, until the end of the day, she never goes out: neither moon nor sun sees her face.
All the devotees who come for prasada see only her holy feet, not her face.
No one can hear her voice; the lotus of her face is always withered, and tears flow from her eyes.
Eating only the remnants on Mother Shachi's plate, she maintains her body only for the sake of service.
When she has time from serving Shachi, she sits in seclusion and ceaselessly chants the Name.
She has a great taste for the nectar of the name of Hari; the crown of chaste women, her body is full of pure love.
Her faith in Your holy feet is deep; by her mercy I came to know her.
She has made a portrait exactly like Your form and consecrated it with the great mantra of loving devotion.
That murti she serves secretly and diligently, having surrendered herself to Your lotus feet.
Even Sri Ananta cannot enumerate her good qualities — how much can I tell You with a single mouth?"
Mahaprabhu said: "Speak no more of this. Give Me the news from the Acharya of Shantipura."
First the pandit told of the Lord's (Advaita's) welfare, and then he delivered His riddle.
Hearing the riddle, Sri Chaitanya said with a smile: "As He permits, so do I accept."
Having said this, Gauranga became stunned, and Svarupa and the other devotees asked Him:
"Tell us, Mahaprabhu, what is the meaning of this riddle? None of us can understand it."
Sri Gauranga said: "This is Advaita Acharya: He has done an unearthly deed — He has made Krishna manifest.
Bhagavan Himself is bound by the rope of His love: by His will Krishna appears and disappears.
Who can understand the meaning of His riddle? He alone understands its meaning; it is not revealed to others."
The sadhus call Him the honoured one among the gods: He is the wish-fulfilling tree of devotion, worshipped by the world.
Hearing this, the devotees were amazed at heart. From that day a change came over Gora.
The divine madness of Sri Radha awoke in Him: "Ah, Lord! Ah, Krishna!" He wept.
In the ecstasy of mahabhava He did not distinguish day from night, and fear settled in the hearts of the devotees.
One day Gora, gazing at Jagannatha, entered the holy temple with the words "Ah, Lord!"
As soon as He entered, the doors closed by themselves, and grave fears arose in the hearts of the devotees.
After some time the doors opened by themselves, and all understood that Gauranga had disappeared.
Although for the devotees Chaitanya has not disappeared, Gaura's companions, following the custom of the world, expressed great grief.
That grief, like the fire of Rudra, of great intensity, burnt the bodies, minds and lives of all beings.
The pastimes of Sri Gauranga are a boundless ocean: Ananta cannot describe even one stream of it.
I am more insignificant than the most insignificant worm: in the bliss of consciousness I tell only a speck of the essence.
Meanwhile my Lord, in an unearthly ecstasy, understood in His heart that Mahaprabhu had disappeared.
The Lord fell into divine madness, lost external awareness and called: "Nimai! Nimai!"
Now He said: "Come here, Nimai, take your books: there is housework — I must go quickly to teach."
Now He said: "I know all Your tricks: tell Me, in what mood did You become Gaura?"
Now He said: "Nimai, stay in My house: if you go to foreign lands, Mother Shachi will grieve."
Now He said: "Gaura, You are the creator of the creator: in the age of Kali You have become the father of the sankirtana of the Name."
And sometimes He said: "You have hidden the treasure of Vraja in Vraja; I search and cannot find it. What tricks are You playing?"
Thus He said aloud many incoherent things; after a long time the Lord's external awareness returned.
Crying "Hari, Hari!", He roared, and all said: "Now the ailment has passed."
Who can understand this pure mahabhava? Only the pure devotees understand it in their hearts.
I, the most insignificant worm, have not a shadow of knowledge: what I saw, its essence I have revealed.
One day Sitanatha, sitting at the gate, was joyfully crying out the names "Hare Krishna."
A devotee who lived in Kshetra came there; seeing him, the Lord seated him respectfully.
Following worldly custom, He, shedding tears, asked very anxiously about Gauranga's welfare.
The Sri Vaishnava said: "I know the news of Chaitanya: the report is that He has disappeared."
Hearing this, the Lord saw everything become empty and, saying "I understood! I understood!", fainted.
After a long time He came to Himself; how many moods appeared in the Lord cannot be described.
Now stupor, now a roar, now rolling on the ground, now with cries of "Gora! Gora!" He wept aloud.
Hearing the weeping, Mother Sita came there; learning the reason, she fainted.
After a long time Sita-devi came to herself and wept loudly, repeating: "Chaitanya!"
Sri Achyuta wept, Krishnadasa wept, Sri Gopaladasa wept, in despair.
Among Sita's sons these three are foremost: they are pure devotees, the lives of the three are given to Gaura.
I have no power to describe their weeping: I have described only a speck of the essence.
A day and a night passed, and the Lord had no external awareness; the Acharya with all His family fasted.
The next day the Lord held a great festival: many brahmanas and Sri Vaishnavas were fed.
Hundreds of poor people received food, and mountains of clothes and cowries were distributed.
In the nectar of the sankirtana of Hari, in the pure waters of the Ganga, Shantipura floated away into the ocean of love.
In its waves many villagers with their families bathed and were immersed.
From that day the Lord, the great master of yoga, ceaselessly meditated on the form of Sri Gauranga.
In a dream Mahaprabhu came to Advaita and said: "Nada, do not grieve in your heart over separation from Me.
Drawn by your love, I have come to your house: you will see Me in the form of Krishna Mishra's son.
And Lord Nityananda-chandra you will find in your house after some days in the form of (another) son of Krishna Mishra.
Your son Krishnadasa, dear to you as life — in his heart I always sport.
He is My eternal devotee, appointed to service; to fulfil his desire I shall appear again."
Having seen this wonderful dream, the Lord was amazed — and on that very day a son was born to Krishna Mishra.
He was the likeness of Sri Gauranga, enchanting the world; seeing his form, the Lord was immersed in love.
His name was Raghunatha; he was a mine of love and, hearing of Gaura's qualities, shed tears.
Then in due time, on the full moon of Krishna's swing festival, a second son was born to Krishna Mishra —
the likeness of Nityananda, an ocean of mercy, who ceaselessly spoke of the glory of Gauranga.
The Lord gave him the name Sri Dolagovinda; hearing it, the devotees cried out the name of Hari in love.
One day Sri Advaita called His sons together and in seclusion spoke to them very gently:
"O children! Calm your minds, all of you, and hear the essence of the dharma of the householder.
Whoever daily performs the sandhya worship and the five great sacrifices is a great sage.
Do not covet another's wife or another's wealth — for that you will suffer both in this world and in the next.
Be merciful to all beings, do no harm; do not blaspheme the sadhus, but praise them.
Plant Sri Tulasi in the courtyard of your house: a house without tulasi is like a cremation ground.
The daily sankirtana of Hari is best of all: it is the atonement for sins, before it Yama himself flees.
Daily association with saints destroys offences; devotion to Krishna is obtained, there is no doubt.
And remember one more word of Mine: do nothing for your own pleasure.
If one leads a householder's life for the service of Krishna, one does not partake of the sin or merit born of deeds.
From selfish deeds worldly desires gradually grow, and by that thread the soul is bound to coming and going in the world.
Therefore give up selfish deeds altogether: if you act for Krishna's sake, your desires will be fulfilled."
Thus He gave many kinds of instruction, and hearing them, Sri Achyuta and the others rejoiced.
Sri Achyuta, Krishna Mishra and Gopaladasa — these three always have jubilation in the service of Krishna.
They always have deep love for Krishna and the Vaishnavas, and Sri Achyuta has complete detachment from the world.
At the Lord's command the waves of the Ganga of love rose, and they began the service of Krishna with various offerings.
Although the minds of all three were wholly given to Krishna, the Lord resolved to entrust the service to Krishna Mishra.
The householder Sri Krishna Mishra is full of pure devotion — the Lord considered him worthy of the service of Krishna.
The son of Labha said to Achyuta: "Listen, My son Sri Achyuta, to My word.
You are My eldest son, the foremost of Vaishnavas: having obtained such a son, I am blessed.
You are supremely pure, in the shastras a Brihaspati, the crown of the righteous, with a most pure mind.
From childhood you have been detached from the world, always devoted to the dharma of supreme detachment.
Therefore you turned away from marriage and considered paltry the pleasures of the external senses so dear to souls.
Therefore I have understood: the service of the Deity and the rites are not your way.
Krishnadasa Mishra, your younger brother, devoted to the gods and brahmanas, the best of Vaishnavas,
most learned, pure of mind, keeper of the treasures of devotion, the crown of lovers, always pure in conduct,
accepts My view and is always obedient to Me; his life is given to Gaura — therefore he is dear to Gaura.
Having married, he has become a householder: in My view he is worthy of the service of Krishna.
All the more since Krishnadasa has two sons — supremely righteous, devoted to Sri Gauranga.
The elder is Raghunatha, the younger Sri Dolagovinda: both find supreme bliss in the service of Sri Krishna.
One day Sriman Raghunatha said to Me: 'How will the word of Veda-Vyasa come true?
(It is said that) in the age of Kali the eighty-four hells will be filled; but Sri Krishna Chaitanya has closed that road —
by the great mantra of the name of Hari He has delivered the souls. Tell me: how will the hells be filled?'
Hearing this, Sri Dolagovinda laughed and said: 'They will be filled with all the sinners who hate Gaura.'
Hearing such words, I was amazed, and since then I know that both are incarnations of gods.
Blessed is My Krishnadasa, blessed are his sons: they are worthy of the service of Sri Madana-Gopala.
He is My own who worships Gauranga: he is fit to serve the treasure of My life.
Therefore I wish to entrust this service to Krishna Mishra. What is your wish?"
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta joyfully said, joining his palms: "As You have commanded, so I too think."
Then Sri Advaita said to Krishna Mishra: "Madana-Gopala is the Lord of My life.
Serve Him with devotion every day; do not allow those turned away from Him to worship Him.
Know that the averse are unbelievers, heretics, Advaitin sannyasis, yogis and jnanis,
those desiring enjoyment and liberation, devoid of the desire for devotion: these non-Vaishnavas I regard as averse to Krishna.
Among Vaishnavas, one who is outside a sampradaya, and among those of a sampradaya, one who does not acknowledge Gauranga —
he is surely averse to Krishna — this I shall determine. And one more word of Mine, listen, Krishnadasa:
those of My own who are evil-minded, who, transgressing My command, go their own way and do not acknowledge Gora —
(know:) Sri Gauranga is My Lord, I am His servant, the dust of His holy feet is My food.
Gora is the Lord of My life, Gora is the One I worship: whoever does not acknowledge that Gauranga is rejected by Me.
Those averse to Krishna are all in a low refuge: they are never fit to serve the Deity (sri-vigraha) of Krishna.
Whoever preserves the true dharma of his father is the real son — such is the word of the Vedas."
Having said this, He insistently entrusted the Deity of Sri Madana-Gopala to Krishna Mishra.
Having received the service of Krishna, Krishna Mishra in the bliss of love prostrated himself at the Lord's lotus feet.
With humble praise he bowed at his mother's feet, and Sita and Advaita both blessed him.
Then he humbly bowed to Sri Achyuta; Achyuta said: "I offer myself to your good fortune.
Krishna wished to show you mercy and revealed that wish through His own devotee,
as Krishna revealed the Vedas through Brahma" — and having said this, he embraced Krishna Mishra.
Gopala said: "Krishna is most merciful: by His mercy He will bring good to the whole family,
as when one waters the root of a tree, the branches, leaves and the rest are filled with joy."
"What good fortune!" — having said this, he bowed to Krishna Mishra, and Krishna Mishra embraced him tightly.
But the Acharya's other sons — Master Balarama and the very mighty Master Jagadisha —
in anger, after consulting with their people, diligently procured another Deity of Krishna,
performed the bathing ceremony and installed that Deity, and held a festival with their own people.
The pastimes of Sri Advaita are an impassable ocean: I have proclaimed only a drop of their essence.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

cc.title: Господь видит во сне Кришну, танцующего расу с Радхой: «Я обрёл Кришну во Вриндаване!» — и Говинда будит Его
cc.summary: Господь увидел во сне Кришну, трижды изогнутого, с флейтой, в жёлтых одеждах и лесной гирлянде, чарующего даже Камадеву, в кругу гопи, танцующего с Радхой, и подумал в блаженстве: наконец Я обрёл Кришну во Вриндаване! Говинда разбудил Его, и Господь опечалился, поняв, что это был сон.

verses.text:
(17) Однажды Шри Чайтанья увидел во сне Кришну, танцующего танец Раса.
трибхан̇га-сундара-деха, муралӣвадана
три изгиба прекрасное тело, с флейтой у лица
пӣта̄мбара, вана-ма̄ла̄, мадана-мохана
желтые одежды, лесная гирлянда, Купидона чарующий
(18) С тремя изгибами на теле и с флейтой у Своих губ, облачённый в жёлтые одежды и украшенный гирляндой из лесных цветов, Кришна был так ошеломляюще прекрасен, что очаровывал даже бога Любви.
ман̣д̣алӣ-бандхе гопӣ-ган̣а карена нартана
в кругу пастушек танцуют
мадхйе ра̄дха̄-саха на̄че враджендра-нандана
посредине с Радхой танцует Враджи царя сын (Кришна)
(19) Сын царя Нанды, Кришна, был в самом центре хоровода юных девушек и танцевал с Радхарани, самой чарующей из пастушек.
декхи’ прабху сеи расе а̄виш̣т̣а хаила̄
увидев Чайтанья то чувством преисполнился
‘вр̣нда̄ване кр̣ш̣н̣а па̄ину’ — эи джн̃а̄на каила̄
во Вриндаване Кришну обрёл это подумал
(20) Заворожённый этой непостижимой красотой, Шри Чайтанья преисполнился блаженством и подумал: «Наконец-то Я обрёл Кришну во Вриндаване!»*
прабхура виламба декхи’ говинда джа̄га̄ила̄
Чайтаньи задержку видя Говинда разбудил
джа̄гиле ‘свапна’-джн̃а̄на хаила, прабху дух̣кхӣ хаила̄
проснувшись сон понял, Чайтанья огорчился
(21) Но, видя, что Шри Чайтанья не проснулся в положенное время, Говинда Его разбудил. Пробудившись, Он понял, что это был всего лишь сон, и сильно опечалился.*
verses.orig:
ত্রিভঙ্গ-সুন্দর-দেহ, মুরলীবদন ৷
পীতাম্বর, বনমালা, মদনমোহন ॥ ১৮ ॥
মণ্ডলীবন্ধে গোপীগণ করেন নর্ত্তন ৷
মধ্যে রাধা-সহ নাচে ব্রজেন্দ্রনন্দন ॥ ১৯ ॥
দেখি’ প্রভু সেই রসে আবিষ্ট হৈলা ৷
‘বৃন্দাবনে কৃষ্ণ পাইনু’ — এই জ্ঞান কৈলা ॥ ২০ ॥
প্রভুর বিলম্ব দেখি’ গোবিন্দ জাগাইলা ৷
জাগিলে ‘স্বপ্ন’-জ্ঞান হৈল, প্রভু দুঃখী হৈলা ॥ ২১ ॥
notes: У ВЧД — «…и подумал Он». «Анубхашья»: «погрузился в эту расу» — всецело ею проникся.
У ВЧД — «Когда Чайтанья пробудился и понял, что это был всего лишь сон, то был сильно огорчён этим».

verses_en.text:
(17) One day, as Mahāprabhu lay asleep, He saw Kṛṣṇa’s rāsa-līlā in a dream.
tribhaṅga-sundara-deha, muralīvadana
bent in three places beautiful body with the flute at His lips
pītāmbara, vana-mālā, madana-mohana
yellow garment forest garland of Madana the enchanter
(18) Kṛṣṇa’s beautiful form was bent in three places, the flute at His lips; He wore yellow cloth and a garland of forest flowers — the enchanter of Madana, the god of love.
maṇḍalī-bandhe gopī-gaṇa karena nartana
in a circle the gopīs were dancing
madhye rādhā-saha nāce vrajendra-nandana
in the middle with Rādhā dances of the king of Vraja the son
(19) The gopīs danced in a circle, and in the middle the son of the king of Vraja danced with Rādhā.
dekhi’ prabhu sei rase āviṣṭa hailā
seeing the Lord in that rasa absorbed became
‘vṛndāvane kṛṣṇa pāinu’ — ei jñāna kailā
in Vṛndāvana Kṛṣṇa I have found this thought He had
(20) Seeing this, the Lord became absorbed in that rasa and thought, “I have found Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana!”
prabhura vilamba dekhi’ govinda jāgāilā
the Lord’s lateness seeing Govinda woke Him
jāgile ‘svapna’-jñāna haila, prabhu duḥkhī hailā
on waking that it was a dream He understood the Lord sorrowful became
(21) When Govinda saw that the Lord was late in rising, he woke Him. On waking, the Lord understood that it had been a dream, and He was filled with sorrow.
